ops.title: CI never runs the Rust core tests with default features
ops.description:
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `cargo test -p cc-transcript-core --no-default-features` (the swift job) and `cargo test -p cc-transcript-py --lib`. No job runs the core crate's own test suite with its default features (`command`, `sqlite`), which is the feature set the published wheel is built with.

Found while landing query_graph observers (yasyf/cc-transcript#55, released as 14.41.0). One regression, `glob_and_regex_kinds_answer_only_as_the_primary_while_the_other_eight_settle_as_observers`, branches on `cfg!(feature = "command")`: without the feature a `has_command` observer reports `null`, with it a definite `false`. CI only ever ran the `null` arm. Other tests in `snapshot_prepared.rs` and `snapshot_projection.rs` have `#[cfg(feature = "command")]` arms with the same exposure.

What covers the default-feature path today, outside this repo's CI: captain-hook's `tests/test_predicate_observers.py::test_the_pinned_producer_settles_planned_siblings_on_one_walk` (runs against the pinned wheel in captain-hook CI) and a probe run on 2026-10-13 against the installed 14.41.0 wheel, which got definite `true` and `false` from `has_command` observers (`/tmp/ram-pressure-refresh-20261012-2335/predicate-delivery-serving-probe.json`, not durable).

Cost to weigh: the no-default-features core suite takes about 8 minutes on the macOS runner (849 tests, 489 s on 2026-10-13). A second full run doubles that. A narrower option is a filtered run of the tests that have feature-dependent arms.

Task e723e1b (Lane C producer) keeps its first criterion pending on this.

ops.text: A CI job runs cc-transcript-core tests with default features, either the whole suite or a named subset that includes every test with a cfg(feature) arm, and it is green on main
The default-feature arm of glob_and_regex_kinds_answer_only_as_the_primary_while_the_other_eight_settle_as_observers runs in that job and passes
